scope: Read-only review of the private guide's pure reference matcher, authenticated client loading, expected-reference UI and focused tests. Exporter/scientific sidecar were outside this review; no guide code changed.
supportedFindings: The client hashes fetched catalog bytes against the build-imported publication manifest and requires its fixed same-origin href. The matcher is explicitly a semantic projection after that byte check; it does not claim scientific authority from pin strings alone.

Only the exact Oct 26 current-polling Senate run and result hash can match; House, the five older fundamentals-only editions, ten other Senate configurations, dates, targets, laws and changed source pins fail closed. The 35 ordered principal-pair rows require matching named candidate IDs, pair denominator, sign, probability, native modal choice, point means, interval endpoints and rule/omitted-option notes. It does not allocate pooled or outside-candidate win mass.

Native draw identity is preserved as 4x10000 equal-weight shared rows. The four distribution summaries keep their original quantiles; expected modal misses and mean absolute margin error are checked against the per-race probabilities/errors. Missing close/decisive probabilities remain null rather than inferred from ranges.

The UI labels errors/ranges as model-implied and internal, explicitly distinguishes them from observed accuracy, says signed error is centered by construction, shows the conditional two-candidate denominator, and assigns no grade or final-result status. The reference cannot be borrowed by a different edition.

findingsToFix.evidence: loadElectionNightForecast calls attachReference for House and every Senate alternative. attachReference always fetches the only Senate standard reference when a publication manifest is passed. If that request fails, House or an alternative displays 'expected-error reference could not be verified' even though no reference exists for its edition. The happy-path alternative test uses a successful fetch and misses this case.
findingsToFix.suggestedChange: Before fetching, return {reference:null,referenceError:null} for forecasts other than the exact eligible Senate current-polling run/result pin (or expose a supported-identity predicate from the matcher). Add a failed-reference-fetch test for House and one Senate alternative that asserts no error banner and no catalog request. This also avoids unnecessary network work.

findingsToFix.evidence: When catalog bytes match the publication manifest but matchElectionNightReference returns null for the exact eligible current-polling edition, attachReference returns reference:null,referenceError:null. UI then says 'No reviewed error reference for this edition,' which hides a build/version mismatch or malformed authenticated catalog as ordinary absence.
findingsToFix.suggestedChange: For the exact eligible run, treat matcher-null as a reference verification error while retaining the forecast. The retry path should remain available. Test a correctly SHA-bound but semantically wrong catalog by changing the manifest test hash to that payload's exact bytes.

nonblockingAbortNote: Resolved by post-digest parent and child signal checks in final client SHA39b2e6dd….
testsAssessed: Author's 9 matcher tests and client/browser tests include actual pin matching, duplicate/stale/foreign edition rejection, row/tie/metric tamper, corrupted optional bytes preserving forecast, reference-fetch cancellation, and UI retry. I inspected their assertions; I did not rerun the full suite while root's build/browser checks are pending.
scopeBoundary: Only one reviewed Senate current-polling V1 reference exists. House expected-error export and any future close/decisive event probabilities require separate pinned contracts.

recheck.evidence: Build-imported publication editions gate optional fetch by exact chamber/run/result SHA; no match returns null without a fetch or error, and duplicate exact matches reject. A declared eligible edition whose authenticated catalog fails semantic matching now produces a reference verification error while keeping the forecast. Tests assert alternative no-fetch and changed authenticated catalog error.
recheck.remainingNonblocking: Post-digest signal.throwIfAborted() would strengthen direct loader cancellation; guide already checks its controller before state updates.

remainingOptionalLoadingLimit: Resolved for ordinary stalled optional network fetch by an 8-second child-controller deadline; cryptographic digest is non-abortable but stale completion is rejected after digest.

finalRecheck.cancellationAndDeadline: Parent signal is forwarded to a child AbortController. Parent and child signals are checked after WebCrypto digest; finally clears the 8-second timer and removes the listener. Timeout yields a reference verification error while retaining the authenticated forecast. Parent cancellation propagates as abort. Tests cover parent cancellation during non-abortable digest and a mocked 8-second deadline.
finalRecheck.scopeLimit: The 8-second bound is on abortable reference network/body work. WebCrypto digest itself is not preempted by abort, but post-digest checks prevent stale fulfillment; an indefinitely stalled digest is outside this timer guarantee.
finalRecheck.rootReportedChecks: 40 unit tests, 10 desktop/mobile browser cases, typecheck and build passed, reported by root; not independently rerun here.
